description: Before-and-after measure of PAPER-95, Cyrano de Bergerac: 10 direct questions, 10 on a new subject after another one, 10 short follow-ups and 5 more precise ones after an admission. Written on 27 November 2026 from passages that no earlier question used, before any search or reply with them, and frozen. The earlier replies of the conversations were written by hand.

items.input: Which painter did Ragueneau say could alone have portrayed you, had he not been dead?
passageQuotes: only Jacques Callot, now dead and gone

items.input: After the evening at the theatre, what did you accept from the buffet-girl?
items.expectedOutput: A few grapes, a glass of water and half a macaroon.

items.input: What was Ragueneau doing at his little table one morning in his shop, before his cooks interrupted him?
items.expectedOutput: Writing poetry with an inspired air, counting on his fingers.
passageQuotes: writing, with an inspired air, at a small table

items.input: When the crowd rushed into the shop to praise you, what did a man of letters with a writing-board ask you for?
items.expectedOutput: A few details (for the Court Gazette).

items.input: When you told the cadets about your night fight, who kept interrupting you with the word nose?
items.expectedOutput: Christian, who had joined that day.

items.input: What revenge on you did Roxane suggest to De Guiche, to keep you out of the war?
items.expectedOutput: Leaving Cyrano behind with the Cadets while the regiment marched to Arras.
passageQuotes: left here with his beloved boon companions

items.input: What did Roxane pretend the postscript of the letter asked to be given to the convent?
passageQuotes: Give twenty pistoles for the Convent

items.input: At the siege, why did you cross the Spanish lines at each dawn?
items.expectedOutput: To send letters to Roxane, as he had promised Christian would write often.
passageQuotes: I promised he should write often

items.input: How was Christian struck down at Arras?
items.expectedOutput: By the first shot of the enemy.
passageQuotes: Struck by first shot of the enemy

items.input: What did the sisters of the convent bake for you?
passageQuotes: We make him pasties of angelica

conversation.content: Which painter did Ragueneau say could alone have portrayed you, had he not been dead?
Jacques Callot alone, said Ragueneau, and he is dead.

items.input: What did you threaten to make the marquises taste if they did not hold their tongues?

conversation.content: After the evening at the theatre, what did you accept from the buffet-girl?
A few grapes, a glass of water and half a macaroon.

items.input: According to you, what is a big nose a sign of?
items.expectedOutput: A soul affable, kind, courteous, liberal and brave.

conversation.content: What was Ragueneau doing at his little table one morning in his shop, before his cooks interrupted him?
Writing verses, counting on his fingers.

items.input: What graceful thing did Ligniere once do as he was leaving church?
items.expectedOutput: He saw his love take holy water and drank the whole stoup, although he hates water.
passageQuotes: drank it all, to the last drop

conversation.content: When the crowd rushed into the shop to praise you, what did a man of letters with a writing-board ask you for?
A few details for his Gazette. I refused.

items.input: Which recipe did Ragueneau recite in verse to the poets?

conversation.content: When you told the cadets about your night fight, who kept interrupting you with the word nose?
A newcomer, Christian.

items.input: Whose battered hats did a cadet bring you strung on his sword?
items.expectedOutput: The hats of the fugitives of the ambush.

conversation.content: What revenge on you did Roxane suggest to De Guiche, to keep you out of the war?
To leave me behind with the Cadets while the regiment marched.

items.input: How did you explain to the duenna the two musicians who followed you?
items.expectedOutput: He had won them from D'Assoucy in a wager over a point of grammar.
passageQuotes: a wager I won of D'Assoucy

conversation.content: What did Roxane pretend the postscript of the letter asked to be given to the convent?
Twenty pistoles.

items.input: When you stopped De Guiche, what did you swear your nose would spout if he squeezed it?

conversation.content: At the siege, why did you cross the Spanish lines at each dawn?
To carry letters: I had promised he would write often.

items.input: What did the old piper play to the starving cadets?
items.expectedOutput: On his flute, airs of their own country (Languedoc, Gascony), which made them homesick.

conversation.content: How was Christian struck down at Arras?
By the enemy's first shot.

items.input: What did De Guiche say as soon as he came upon the cadets after their feast?

conversation.content: What did the sisters of the convent bake for you?
Pasties of angelica, the good sisters.

items.input: What did the Duke warn Le Bret had been said at the Queen's card-play?
items.expectedOutput: That Cyrano may die by accident.

conversation.content: Who had been posted that night to attack Ligniere?
A hundred men.

items.input: And where were they waiting?

conversation.content: What did a bore ask you after the duel, about a great man to shield you?
Whether I had a patron. I have none.

items.input: What did you say protects you instead?

conversation.content: Why did you hate Montfleury?
Because he dared to raise his eyes to her.

items.input: What did it look like to you when he did?
items.expectedOutput: A slug crawling over a flower's petals.

conversation.content: As children, where did you use to play with Roxane?
At Bergerac, by the lake-side.

items.input: What did you cut there, and what for?
passageQuotes: the reeds you cut to make your swords

conversation.content: Under Roxane's balcony, who first spoke to her, and haltingly?
Christian.

items.input: And what did you do about it?
items.expectedOutput: Drew him under the balcony and slipped into his place to speak for him.

conversation.content: Which farewell letter had you already written before the last battle?
Christian's, to Roxane.

items.input: What did he notice on it?

conversation.content: How did Roxane reach the army at Arras?
Through the Spanish lines, in her carriage.

items.input: What did she answer when they asked where she was going?
items.expectedOutput: That she was going to see her lover.
passageQuotes: I go to see my lover

conversation.content: Who drove Roxane's carriage into the camp?
Ragueneau!

items.input: What did he first draw from under the seat?
passageQuotes: The galantine passes from hand to hand

conversation.content: At the siege, how often did you send Roxane letters in Christian's name?
Every day.

items.input: And how many times a day?

conversation.content: When you swooned on your last visit, what did you say had caused it?
The old wound of Arras.

items.input: And what did you then ask her to let you read?
passageQuotes: His letter! Ah! you promised me one day

conversation.content: What would you refuse to do to get on in the world?
Faith, my memory fails me there. Ask me something more precise.

items.input: I mean when Le Bret urged you to find a patron: which plant did you refuse to be like, climbing round a tree?
passageQuotes: like the crawling ivy round a tree

conversation.content: What did Roxane plan for Christian that evening?
Faith, my memory fails me there. Ask me something more precise.

items.input: I mean what she told you at her door, in secret: what would she ask him to speak to her about?
items.expectedOutput: Love, giving rein to his fancy.
passageQuotes: Speak to me of love, and speak splendidly

conversation.content: What did you say to Roxane in the dusk?
Faith, my memory fails me there. Ask me something more precise.

items.input: I mean when you spoke under the balcony of your fear of ridicule: instead of aiming at a star, what did you say you gather?

conversation.content: How did you say one could travel up there?
Faith, my memory fails me there. Ask me something more precise.

items.input: I mean the method with an iron platform that you told De Guiche: what do you throw in the air?
passageQuotes: To throw a magnet in the air

conversation.content: What news did you bring Roxane on your last visit?
Faith, my memory fails me there. Ask me something more precise.

items.input: I mean in your gazette, for the first Saturday: what had the King eaten too much of?
